knowledge_point.title: Determining the Critical Points of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}\left(u - 4\right)^{2} \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=\left(u - 4\right)^{2},\,y(u,v,w)=v,\,z(u,v,w)=w.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =2 u - 8 & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}2 u - 8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(2 u - 8)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(2 u - 8)(1\cdot(1)-(0)\cdot(0)) \\  & =2 \left(u - 4\right).\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ 2 \left(u - 4\right) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The critical points lie on the plane $u - 4=0.$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: The critical points lie on the plane $v - 4=0.$

The critical points lie on the plane $u=0.$

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}u - v + 2 w \\ - 4 u^{2} + v \\ - 4 u^{2} + 3 u + w\end{bmatrix}.
$$

For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=u - v + 2 w,\,y(u,v,w)=- 4 u^{2} + v,\,z(u,v,w)=- 4 u^{2} + 3 u + w.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =1 & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =-1 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =2 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =- 8 u & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =3 - 8 u & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 \\ - 8 u & 1 & 0 \\ 3 - 8 u & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}+(1)\begin{vmatrix}- 8 u & 0 \\ 3 - 8 u & 1\end{vmatrix}+(2)\begin{vmatrix}- 8 u & 1 \\ 3 - 8 u & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1)(1\cdot(1)-(0)\cdot(0))+(1)(- 8 u\cdot(1)-(0)\cdot(3 - 8 u))+(2)(- 8 u\cdot(0)-(1)\cdot(3 - 8 u)) \\  & =8 u - 5.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ 8 u - 5 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The critical points lie on the plane $8 u - 5=0.$

$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=u v,\,y(u,v,w)=5 u + 7 v,\,z(u,v,w)=w.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =v & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =u & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =5 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =7 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =1\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ - 5 u + 7 v & =0.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}(u-1)(v+2) \\ (u-1)+(v+2) \\ (w+1)\end{bmatrix}.

question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=(u-1)(v+2),\,y(u,v,w)=(u-1)+(v+2),\,z(u,v,w)=(w+1).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =(v+2) & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =(u-1) & \,\frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂w} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}(v+2) & (u-1) & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =1\begin{vmatrix}(v+2) & (u-1) \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(v+2)-(u-1).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ (v+2)-(u-1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $(v+2)-(u-1)=0$ defines the plane $(v+2)=(u-1)..$

question.:question/problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}(u-1)+2(w+1) \\ (v+2)-(u-1) \\ (u-1)(w+1)\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=(u-1)+2(w+1),\,y(u,v,w)=(v+2)-(u-1),\,z(u,v,w)=(u-1)(w+1).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂w} & =2 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =(w+1) & \,\frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂w} & =(u-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ (w+1) & 0 & (u-1)\end{vmatrix} \\  & =1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & (u-1)\end{vmatrix}+2\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 1 \\ (w+1) & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =1((u-1)-0)+2(0-(w+1)) \\  & =(u-1)-2(w+1).\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ (u-1)-2(w+1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $(u-1)-2(w+1)=0$ defines the plane $(u-1)=2(w+1).$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $u - 1=0.$
The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $u + 2 w + 1=0.$
The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $u - w - 2=0.$
The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $w + 1=0.$
The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $u - 2 w - 3=0.$

question.:question/problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{(u-1)} \\ (v+2)(w+1) \\ (u-1)+(w+1)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Assume $u>1$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=\sqrt{(u-1)},\,y(u,v,w)=(v+2)(w+1),\,z(u,v,w)=(u-1)+(w+1).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{(u-1)}} & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =(w+1) & \,\frac{∂y}{∂w} & =(v+2) \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂w} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{(u-1)}} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & (w+1) & (v+2) \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{(u-1)}}\begin{vmatrix}(w+1) & (v+2) \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}0 & 0 \\ (w+1) & (v+2)\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{(u-1)}}((w+1)-0)+0 \\  & =\frac{(w+1)}{2\sqrt{(u-1)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ \frac{(w+1)}{2\sqrt{(u-1)}} & =0 \\ (w+1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $(w+1)=0$ defines the plane $(w+1)=0,$ i.e., plane $w=-1$.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $v w + v + 2 w + 2=0.$
The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $v + 2=0.$
The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $u - 1=0.$
The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $u + w=0.$
The critical points are exactly the domain points satisfying $w + 1=0.$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & ={e}^{(u-1)} & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & ={e}^{(u-1)+(w+1)} & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂w} & ={e}^{(u-1)+(w+1)} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =(v+2) & \,\frac{∂z}{∂v} & =(u-1) & \,\frac{∂z}{∂w} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}{e}^{(u-1)} & 0 & 0 \\ {e}^{(u-1)+(w+1)} & 0 & {e}^{(u-1)+(w+1)} \\ (v+2) & (u-1) & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & ={e}^{(u-1)}\begin{vmatrix}0 & {e}^{(u-1)+(w+1)} \\ (u-1) & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & ={e}^{(u-1)}(0-(u-1){e}^{(u-1)+(w+1)}) \\  & =-(u-1){e}^{2(u-1)+(w+1)}.\end{aligned}

$$
